verdicts.quote: in **one atomic commit**: afterwards either all N users exist or none does.
headline "No users were created", file-error message **or** a problem table (row, line, column, message) with the truncation notice when applicable
same normalised email as an earlier row → `EMAIL_DUPLICATE_IN_FILE` with `first_row` (the earliest row with that syntactically valid email); else already belongs to an existing user → `EMAIL_EXISTS`.
Imported user cannot be admin: a header `email,name,role` is refused (R-2.AC3); no accepted file can produce a user with the admin role.
The import operation succeeds only for a signed-in user who is an admin **at the time of the request**.
verdicts.missing: The rule identifies eligible importers but does not say how import authority relates to permission to create a single user.

verdicts.quote: Header: first non-blank record; names matched case-insensitively after trimming; must be exactly `email` and `name`, each once, in any order. … A file with no records at all → `HEADER_INVALID`.
valid UTF-8, an optional leading byte-order mark is removed … records end in LF or CRLF; a field may be quoted with `"`, in which case it may contain commas, line breaks and doubled quotes
A store failure injected on the 2nd of 2 inserts in V1's commit → `failed`, users 4 afterwards (not 5). … The import sets **no credentials and sends no email**.
A file larger than **2,097,152 bytes** is rejected `TOO_LARGE`; a file with more than **5,000 data rows** is rejected `TOO_MANY_ROWS`.
A file with no records at all → `HEADER_INVALID`. Header only → `NO_ROWS`. … One row (N = 1) and 5,000 rows (N = max) behave identically.
Re-uploading a file whose import was committed changes nothing: every row is `EMAIL_EXISTS`.
The import is **one synchronous request/response**; the response is sent only after the outcome is final. … "{n} user(s) created", all created emails, "Import another file"
verdicts.missing: The screen reports completion, but even the largest accepted file is processed synchronously. Background processing for large files is explicitly excluded.

verdicts.quote: The import sets **no credentials and sends no email**.
how imported users obtain a way to sign in is not specified; PD-5 imports them without credentials.
verdicts.missing: The initial active or pending status and the steps a new user takes to sign in for the first time are unspecified.

verdicts.quote: live only in the request's memory (or an equivalent transient scope) and are discarded when the response is sent … and are visible only to the uploading admin's request.

timestamp, actor id (or `anonymous`), outcome, file error code if any, data rows parsed, created count, errors total, duration. It never contains emails, names, any cell value, file content or the file name.
verdicts.missing: The audit identifies the actor, time and counts. It provides no identifier linking an attempt to the particular file or accounts imported.

verdicts.quote: file or row problems → `rejected`, nothing created; screen Rejected; the admin fixes the file and starts F-1 again.
verdicts.missing: The recovery path is a whole-file retry. The specification gives no cancellation action or cancellation outcome for an in-flight import, and no retry limited to failed rows.

verdicts.quote: the only hard bound is the host's request timeout, which is unknown (G-5). … button disabled and relabelled "Importing…", indeterminate progress, chooser disabled
verdicts.missing: The admin sees progress, but the maximum duration for a 5,000-row file depends on a timeout whose value is unresolved.

verdicts.quote: existing users are never modified. … the same defaults as a user created one at a time by the existing product path
verdicts.missing: The import preserves existing accounts and reuses single-user defaults. There is no requirement that the existing manual creation flow continue to work exactly as before.

verdicts.quote: begins with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is stored verbatim; neutralising such values is the duty of any future CSV/spreadsheet export … email of 254 characters accepted, 255 rejected; name of 255 accepted, 256 rejected
